jobs.title: Senior Director, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
Our Company Background & Culture

UPP is the first pension plan of its kind in Ontario’s university sector, proudly serving over 46,000 members across six universities and nineteen sector organizations. Our purpose is to bring greater retirement peace of mind to the university sector by investing with integrity and serving members with care. As a sector-wide plan designed for growth, our doors are open to all Ontario universities.
UPP is recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for 2026. Together, we’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact.
Our culture is intentionally welcoming and purposefully rooted in equity, diversity, inclusion, and reconciliation (EDI&R). We believe diverse teams, perspectives, and lived experiences contribute to better decisions and a better workplace.
As a pension plan, UPP approaches investing through a long-term lens to generate and safeguard value. Our commitment to investing responsibly accounts for material risks that impact our investment portfolio to generate sufficient risk-adjusted returns to meet the pension needs of our members.
Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other.
THE ROLE

We are seeking a forward-looking Senior Director, Data & Analytics to lead and evolve UPP’s enterprise data capabilities. Reporting to the Managing Director, Data and Technology, this role will work with business and technology leaders to improve how data is governed, integrated, managed and used across UPP. Its scope includes data in UPP’s enterprise data hub and across the broader cloud solutions ecosystem, including Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The Senior Director will help ensure data is trusted, accessible and fit for business reporting, analytics, automation and emerging AI workloads.
This is an opportunity for an experienced data leader to shape an important enterprise capability and help UPP make better use of its data as the organization grows.
This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (two days per week in-office).
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Specific Accountabilities

The Senior Director, Data & Analytics will lead and evolve UPP’s data capabilities, including the following:
Develop and evolve UPP’s enterprise data strategy and practices so data is well governed, reliable, discoverable and useful across the organization.
Lead and develop a high-performing team responsible for data quality, data engineering, data integration, data operations and analytics enablement.
Establish data standards and practices in partnership with business data owners, Architecture, Cybersecurity and other technology teams.
Guide the use of cloud-based data capabilities, including GCP, to support reliable data integration, reporting and analytics. Improve data quality, access, lineage and governance so data is ready for responsible automation and AI workloads, in partnership with the teams accountable for AI platforms, architecture, privacy and cybersecurity.
Partner with business and technology leaders to prioritize data needs and enable trusted, data-informed decisions. Establish the access patterns, tools, standards, training and controls that allow business users, including citizen data users, to work with data safely and at scale.
Improve the reliability, quality, reuse and maintainability of data integration and transformation flows that support key processes, including pension data conversion, regular employer reporting, and Finance reporting and analysis.
Leverage leading frameworks (such as DCAM) to continually mature and evolve the data strategy and frequently self-asses the capabilities for progress
Define and communicate data priorities, target capabilities and roadmaps, aligning plans with enterprise needs and available capacity.
Research and establish peer connections to understand industry trends and their applicability to support data plans and strategies for the enterprise
Explain the value of trusted data and sound data management practices to technical and non-technical audiences.
Oversee UPP’s data catalog and related metadata practices, working with Architecture and data owners to improve data discoverability and stewardship.
Contribute to UPP’s reputation as a respectful employer, partner, and participant in the financial sector

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of demonstrated experience developing and leading enterprise data capabilities, including data governance, data engineering, integration, data operations and analytics.
CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional) or an equivalent qualification is an asset.
Significant progressive experience in data management, including data governance, architecture, integration, data quality, metadata and analytics.
Experience leading data teams or capabilities in a cloud-based environment, with sufficient technical understanding of data platforms, databases, integration and transformation tools, analytics and visualization to set direction and make informed decisions. Experience with GCP or comparable cloud data platforms is an asset.
Understanding of relational and non-relational data and the considerations involved in integrating and governing different data types.
Experience working across complex business domains; experience in pensions, investments or financial services is an asset.
Experience designing and evolving cloud-based data capabilities in partnership with internal teams and external service providers.
Working knowledge of analytics methods and the interpretation of quantitative information.

ATTRIBUTES

Excellent written and verbal communications
Ability to design and improve repeatable data practices
Ability to drive outcomes through collaboration across teams and contributors
Ability to engage and align business users, data owners and technology partners.
Ability to effectively identify emerging technologies, trends, standards, and products that have a strong potential to better enable UPP business units
Ability to enable consistent, governed data use at scale.

LIFE AT UPP

Do work that matters.
We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come.
Stronger together.
Collaboration is how UPP was born, and it’s how we work with each other and our partners day in, day out. No one at UPP is just a number (even if they are excellent at math) and every win is a shared win.
Grow every day.
You’ll have the opportunity to work on unique, once-in-a-career projects that maximize your skill set and probably teach you some new ones—at any stage in your career.
Prioritize wellness.
At UPP, wellness takes many forms. Ultimately, it’s about ensuring our people are cared for in the ways that matter to them. Check out some highlights of our inclusive employee-focused benefits program including:
Defined benefit pension plan
Flexible hybrid work model
Paid time off – vacations, personal days and wellness days
Work remotely up to eight weeks/year
Comprehensive group benefits including medical, dental, vision, etc.
Extended paramedical and mental health service coverage
Health care and lifestyle spending accounts
Fertility treatments, paid parental leave, and gender affirmation coverage
Education Assistance program

This posting will remain open for a minimum of seven (7) days and will remain open until a sufficient number of qualified applications are received or finalist candidates have been identified.
Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support certain stages of the recruitment process, including sourcing, screening, and assessment. All hiring decisions involve human review and intervention by UPP employees.
UPP enthusiastically welcomes applications from all qualified applicants and especially invites people with lived experience as an Indigenous person, a person with a disability or as a member of another Human Rights Code protected group that faces barriers to employment to apply. Our goal is to create a barrier-free experience for every candidate throughout the recruitment process.

UPP respects your privacy. For information on how UPP handles the personal information you provide during the application process, please see our Job Applicant Privacy Statement.

jobs.title: Chief Courts Information Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

Affinity Earn

Know someone who’s great for this, or any of our open roles? Earn up to $4,000/year for each successful referral through Affinity Earn. You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. Learn about our referral program at https://affinity-group.ca/earn/ or browse our jobs & follow us at https://www.linkedin.com/company/affinity-staffing/jobs/

About Affinity

Affinity Group is a technology and business consulting and services company. We believe in creating long term relationships between clients and consultants that foster a mutually beneficial partnership. Affinity is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

For more information on Affinity, please visit www.affinity-group.ca

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Company Description

AI can be trusted, but only with the right measures, mitigations and third party validation. NuEnergy.ai ensures effective and practical AI governance by helping customers establish responsible AI trust guardrails, manage accountability for AI impacts, and maintain transparent AI trust scores. NuEnergy.ai provides organizations with a comprehensive third-party AI Trust Process, a powerful AI Trust Platform (the NuEnergy.ai Machine Trust Platform™), and mentoring by a knowledgeable AI Trust Faculty. Founded in 2018, NuEnergy.ai serves global AI governance customers from headquarters in Ottawa, Canada.

Why work with us:

NuEnergy.ai believes in bringing out the best of every employee’s strengths, skills and potential. We work together to help you achieve your professional and personal aspirations. Our culture promises employees an environment of equal opportunity and a strong sense of community. When you win, we all win.

Position Overview 

The VP, Finance and Administration will own NuEnergy.ai’s financial health and the administrative systems that keep the company running, from planning and reporting through to payroll, contracts and compliance. This role is ideal for a hands-on finance leader who is as comfortable doing the work as setting the direction: building the model, closing the books and fixing the process, not only overseeing it. You will partner with the CEO on strategy and fundraising, support the board with clear and timely reporting, and work with Sales, Program Delivery and Product to make sure growth is well planned and well governed.

Key Responsibilities 

Financial strategy and planning

Lead annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning and rolling forecasts, linked to company strategy and growth plans
Manage cash flow, runway and working capital, and give the CEO early visibility of risks and options
Build and maintain financial models to support pricing, new offerings, hiring plans and investment decisions

Accounting, reporting and controls

Own month-end and year-end close, ensuring accurate and timely financial statements
Prepare monthly management reports and board-ready financial packages with clear commentary
Lead the annual review or audit engagement with external accountants
Design and maintain internal controls, approval authorities and finance policies suited to a growing company

Tax, funding and compliance

Oversee corporate tax, GST/HST, payroll remittances and other federal and provincial filings, working with external advisors
Manage government funding and tax credit programs, including SR&ED and IRAP, from application through claims and reporting
Ensure compliance with funding agreements, contract terms and statutory obligations

Fundraising and investor relations

Support the CEO on fundraising, including financial models, data rooms, due diligence and investor reporting
Maintain the cap table and corporate records in coordination with legal counsel
Manage banking, credit and insurance relationships

Administration and people operations

Oversee payroll, benefits administration and HR policies, ensuring compliance with Ontario employment standards and other applicable legislation for a team of both full-time and part-time employees and contractors that is distributed across Canada and the United States
Manage contracts administration, including customer, vendor and contractor agreements, in coordination with legal counsel
Support public-sector procurement requirements, including bid financials, vendor registrations and security clearance processes
Oversee office, IT and vendor administration, and select and improve the finance and administrative tools the company relies on.

Leadership and collaboration

Work with cross-functional teams (Sales, Product Management, Software Development, Program Delivery) to support pricing, proposals, resourcing and delivery margins
Provide regular updates to leadership and the board on financial performance, risks and progress
Build a working understanding of AI governance and NuEnergy.ai’s offerings, so finance decisions reflect how the business creates value
Contribute to fostering a collaborative and results-oriented team culture, consistent with NuEnergy.ai’s values of trust, transparency, and principled, ethical AI

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or Business Administration, or a related field
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing
Minimum 10+ years of progressive experience in finance, accounting and administration, including at least 5 years in a senior finance leadership role (Controller, Director of Finance, VP Finance or equivalent)
Hands-on experience owning the full accounting cycle, budgeting, forecasting and cash management in a growing organization
Working knowledge of Canadian tax, payroll and employment standards, and of ASPE and/or IFRS
A proven track record of execution: building processes from the ground up, delivering on deadlines and following through with minimal direction
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain financial information clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, the board and investors
High integrity and sound judgement in handling confidential information
Ability to work constructively in an office team environment, as well as a virtual team environment
Ability to travel as needed
Willing to obtain Government of Canada security clearance and background check
We’re a bring-your-own-device team, so you’ll use your own laptop and cellphone for work.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or other graduate degree in finance or business
Experience in a technology, SaaS or professional services company, ideally at start-up or scale-up stage
Experience with SR&ED, IRAP and other government funding programs
Experience supporting equity or debt fundraising, board reporting and investor relations
Experience with government or public-sector contracts and procurement
Experience with US operations, including cross-border tax and payroll
Experience implementing or improving cloud accounting, payroll and expense management systems

Job Type
: Full Time

Location:
Based in the Ottawa area, with a willingness to travel for occasional in-person meetings as needed to include hybrid work with weekly in-person time.  

Why NuEnergy.ai?

Join us in our mission to build trust in AI. At NuEnergy.ai, we offer a collaborative work environment, opportunities for growth, and the chance to be part of a team that is shaping the future of AI governance.

How to Apply?

Interested candidates should submit a resume and a cover letter outlining their qualifications and explaining their interest in this position. Please email your resume to careers@nuenergy.ai.
NuEnergy.ai is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

Please note that we thank all applicants for their interest in NuEnergy.ai and will keep resumes on file but will only contact qualified candidates for interviews.

jobs.title: Directeur Financier | Finance Director
jobs.description:
Description

Qui sommes-nous : Manos

Manos Software Group fait partie de Valsoft Corporation, un investisseur à long terme dans les entreprises de logiciels de marchés verticaux. Valsoft acquiert et exploite des sociétés de logiciels avec une vision de détention permanente, en mettant l’accent sur l’autonomie, une croissance disciplinée et la création de valeur à long terme. Manos se concentre sur des secteurs connexes à la santé, notamment les logiciels dentaires, médicaux et vétérinaires.

Description Du Poste

Dans le cadre de l’expansion continue de notre portefeuille d’entreprises de logiciels spécialisés par secteur d’activité, nous recherchons une personne dynamique et expérimentée pour rejoindre notre équipe en tant que Directeur.trice Financier·ère. Relevant directement de l’un des Partenaires d’Investissement, la personne retenue sera responsable de la supervision de la performance financière et du développement stratégique de notre portefeuille. Ce rôle implique une prise en charge complète de la planification financière, du reporting et de la gestion de la performance.

La personne idéale est un.e leader stratégique doté.e d’une forte expertise financière, capable de favoriser l’excellence opérationnelle, d’optimiser la rentabilité et d’assurer un flux de trésorerie positif. Cette personne travaillera en étroite collaboration avec des équipes interfonctionnelles, en favorisant la coopération pour exécuter avec succès les stratégies d’entreprise tout en maintenant des contrôles financiers rigoureux et une conformité exemplaire.

Responsabilités principales

Piloter la planification financière en analysant la performance et les risques du portefeuille
Définir les objectifs et superviser l’ensemble du personnel comptable et financier (comptabilité, FP&A, comptes clients, comptes fournisseurs)
Préparer les rapports financiers mensuels, trimestriels et annuels
Élaborer et gérer les prévisions financières mensuelles, trimestrielles et annuelles ; suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPIs)
Surveiller et analyser les performances pour identifier des axes d’amélioration et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action permettant d’atteindre ou de dépasser les objectifs financiers
Suivre la santé financière du portefeuille et garantir un flux de trésorerie positif
Diriger et organiser les audits légaux annuels, en veillant au respect de toutes les obligations réglementaires
Développer des stratégies pour améliorer la rentabilité et le retour sur investissement
Superviser et réviser les activités comptables, y compris la fiscalité et la conformité
Veiller à l’efficacité des contrôles financiers internes et évaluer en continu les politiques et procédures en place
Collaborer avec l’équipe chargée de l’intégration des entreprises nouvellement acquises, notamment pour la production des bilans d’ouverture, des états financiers complets, et pour assurer leur intégration aux processus financiers de Valsoft
Maintenir une communication régulière avec le département Finance du groupe
Participer activement aux processus d’acquisition et de cession d’entreprises
Accomplir toutes autres responsabilités confiées par l’employeur, que la personne s’engage à exécuter avec diligence, conformément aux termes de l’accord

Prêt(e) à joindre une équipe collaborative et innovante où vous pourrez avoir un impact immédiat?

#Manos

Manos Overview

Manos Software Group is part of Valsoft Corporation, a long-term investor in vertical market software businesses. Valsoft acquires and operates software companies with a permanent ownership mindset, emphasizing autonomy, disciplined growth, and long-term value creation. Manos focuses on healthcare-adjacent verticals, including dental, medical, and veterinary software.

Position Description

As we continue to expand our portfolio of vertical market software businesses, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced professional to join our team as Finance Director. Reporting directly to one of our Investment Partners, the Finance Director will be responsible for overseeing the financial performance and strategic development of our portfolio. This role involves full ownership and accountability for financial planning, reporting, and performance management. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader with a strong financial acumen, capable of driving operational excellence, optimizing profitability, and ensuring positive cash flow. They will work closely with cross-functional teams, fostering collaboration to execute business strategies successfully while maintaining rigorous financial controls and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Drive the financial planning of the company by analyzing portfolio performance and risks
Set targets for and supervise all accounting and finance personnel (Accounting, FP&A, AR, AP)
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports
Build and manage monthly, quarterly, and annual forecasts; track KPIs
Monitor and analyze performance strategies to identify areas of opportunity and implement action plans to meet or exceed financial targets
Monitor the financial health of the portfolio and ensure positive cash flow
Lead and organize annual statutory audits and ensure all required filings are completed
Develop strategies to increase return on investment and profitability
Oversee and review accounting tasks, including tax and compliance
Ensure effective financial internal controls and continuously evaluate established policies and procedures
Collaborate with the integration team of newly acquired companies by producing opening balances, complete financials, and onboarding on Valsoft finance procedures
Maintain high-level interaction with the corporate finance department
Actively participate in processes related to the sale or acquisition of companies
Perform all other applicable responsibilities as delegated by the Employer, which the Employee agrees to carry out diligently under the terms of the Agreement

Ready to join a collaborative and innovative team where you can make an immediate impact?

jobs.title: AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Corporate Strategy & Enablement Team’s focus is to support Sun Life in achieving and maintaining a position of sustainable strategic advantage and growth in the long term. It has a broad focus on enterprise topics that span all Business Groups and geographic markets where Sun Life operates.

The AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement will report to the VP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement. The AVP will be responsible for ongoing delivery of internal strategy design and execution, and the annual strategic planning cycle, working effectively with teams across Sun Life to deliver strategy projects and proactively monitor and analyze trends. The successful candidate will work in a fast-paced, team-first environment with a focus on driving strategy and enablement project delivery, engaging senior leaders across Sun Life to solve key strategic questions/issues and structuring quantitative and qualitative analysis to solve critical strategic questions. The AVP will manage a small high performing team, acting as a coach and mentor through project work and team development opportunities.

What will you do:

Strategy development and planning:

Translate ambiguous issues into clear problem statements and hypotheses
Conduct quantitative (e.g., financial modeling, market sizing) and qualitative (e.g., benchmarking, expert synthesis) analysis
Develop and execute analysis plans using internal and external data sources

Strategy and enablement project delivery:

Define scope, design approach, and lead execution of strategy projects
Manage all project workstreams and coordinate across team members to ensure timely delivery
Present findings and facilitate discussions with senior management, including implementation planning

Trends and competitive intelligence:

Monitor industry trends, competitor actions, and market developments
Curate insights and identify implications for Sun Life’s strategy
Proactively share relevant patterns and themes with internal stakeholders

Communication and stakeholder engagement:

Effectively communicate insights, ideas, and strategies clearly & concisely to an executive level audience
Develop and maintain cross-functional relationships across the organization to identify emerging needs and opportunities
Facilitate working sessions with senior executives, including Sun Life’s Executive Team

People leadership and team development:

Manage a team of high-performing Directors & Senior Consultants
Mentor team members through apprenticeship and coaching
Foster a collaborative and learning-oriented team culture
Contribute to the development and success of the team and our practices

What do you need to succeed:

10+ years of relevant business experience, ideally within insurance or financial services
Strong understanding of at least one Sun Life business area (e.g. asset management, insurance, wealth management) and geographic markets (Canada, US, Asia)
Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills; able to effectively collaborate with multiple stakeholders across multiple teams
Able to work independently on assignments with appropriate judgment
Ability to coach team members on projects, providing guidance on analysis and deliverables
Proven ability to lead and develop a small team of high-performing professionals, including guiding project execution, driving accountability, and conducting performance and career development conversations

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
Most financial reporting functions are measured by whether deadlines are met. That’s important, but this role gets to decide what excellence looks like while meeting deadlines.

With accountability for external reporting and technical accounting, the Senior Director, Financial Reporting will play a defining role in advancing the reporting function of a Canadian-headquartered public manufacturing company. Reporting to the VP, Finance, this leader will oversee the full reporting cycle and strengthen the processes, controls, technical expertise and team required to support its continued evolution.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can deliver against current reporting requirements while strengthening the function for the future. The successful candidate will bring experience from a rigorous public company reporting environment and the judgment to apply that experience within a Finance organization that continues to evolve.

The Mandate

The Senior Director will have end-to-end responsibility for quarterly and annual public company reporting under IFRS, ensuring financial statements, disclosures and supporting documentation meet the standards required of a public company.

The role will also serve as a key technical accounting resource across Finance, providing guidance on complex and non-routine matters and ensuring accounting positions are well considered, documented and communicated.

Key responsibilities include:
Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting, including the preparation and review of external financial statements and disclosures under IFRS.
Own the reporting process from planning through review and completion, with clear accountability for quality, accuracy and timelines.
Provide technical accounting leadership across Finance, interpreting and applying IFRS to complex and judgmental matters.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos covering areas such as goodwill, impairment and significant accounting estimates.
Support potential US GAAP considerations and the requirements associated with a potential conversion.
Provide accounting support for M&A transactions, integrations and divestitures as they arise.
Lead reporting and technical accounting discussions with external auditors, ensuring issues are properly analyzed, documented and resolved.
Strengthen reporting processes, controls, documentation and review standards.
Identify opportunities to create greater consistency, efficiency and discipline across the reporting function.
Lead, coach and develop the team, including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Partner closely with Finance and Tax on accounting and reporting matters.
Build effective relationships with senior leaders and C-suite stakeholders, communicating complex issues clearly and credibly.

What You Bring

You are a CPA/CA with progressive public company financial reporting experience and strong technical accounting capability. You understand the discipline required in a public company environment and have experience taking ownership of a reporting process from beginning to end.

Your background includes:
CPA/CA designation, ideally with a foundation in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience with direct ownership of quarterly and annual reporting.
Strong IFRS technical accounting expertise and experience applying guidance to complex accounting matters.
Experience preparing and reviewing technical accounting memos on significant, judgmental and non-routine issues.
The technical depth and judgment required to support potential US GAAP conversion requirements.
Experience working directly with external auditors and supporting accounting positions through clear analysis and documentation.
M&A-related accounting experience, including exposure to integrations and divestitures, considered a strong asset.
A track record of improving reporting processes, controls and standards.
Proven people leadership experience, including coaching, development and performance management.
Comfort working in a fast-paced environment where processes and capabilities continue to be refined.

How You Lead

You bring the technical credibility to navigate complex accounting matters and the business judgment to understand their broader implications. You are comfortable operating in the detail, but you know when to step back, engage others and move an issue toward resolution.

Your leadership is reflected in how you:
Establish and maintain a high standard for reporting quality.
Apply sound judgment when accounting guidance requires thoughtful interpretation.
Communicate complex matters clearly to audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge.
Build trusted relationships across the reporting team, Finance, Tax, external auditors and the C-suite.
Create accountability through clear expectations, ongoing feedback and meaningful coaching.
Develop people while addressing performance concerns directly and fairly.

The Opportunity

For someone who has developed their experience in a strong public company reporting environment, this role provides the opportunity to take on a broader leadership mandate within a manufacturing business headquartered in Canada.

The Senior Director will have the scope to improve how the reporting function operates, strengthen its technical accounting capability, develop the team and introduce the structure needed to support the organization as it evolves.

It is a role for a financial reporting leader who enjoys the rigor of public company reporting but also wants the opportunity to build, improve and leave the function stronger.

Apply in confidence.

new_jobs.title: AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement
new_jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Corporate Strategy & Enablement Team’s focus is to support Sun Life in achieving and maintaining a position of sustainable strategic advantage and growth in the long term. It has a broad focus on enterprise topics that span all Business Groups and geographic markets where Sun Life operates.

The AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement will report to the VP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement. The AVP will be responsible for ongoing delivery of internal strategy design and execution, and the annual strategic planning cycle, working effectively with teams across Sun Life to deliver strategy projects and proactively monitor and analyze trends. The successful candidate will work in a fast-paced, team-first environment with a focus on driving strategy and enablement project delivery, engaging senior leaders across Sun Life to solve key strategic questions/issues and structuring quantitative and qualitative analysis to solve critical strategic questions. The AVP will manage a small high performing team, acting as a coach and mentor through project work and team development opportunities.

What will you do:

Strategy development and planning:

Translate ambiguous issues into clear problem statements and hypotheses
Conduct quantitative (e.g., financial modeling, market sizing) and qualitative (e.g., benchmarking, expert synthesis) analysis
Develop and execute analysis plans using internal and external data sources

Strategy and enablement project delivery:

Define scope, design approach, and lead execution of strategy projects
Manage all project workstreams and coordinate across team members to ensure timely delivery
Present findings and facilitate discussions with senior management, including implementation planning

Trends and competitive intelligence:

Monitor industry trends, competitor actions, and market developments
Curate insights and identify implications for Sun Life’s strategy
Proactively share relevant patterns and themes with internal stakeholders

Communication and stakeholder engagement:

Effectively communicate insights, ideas, and strategies clearly & concisely to an executive level audience
Develop and maintain cross-functional relationships across the organization to identify emerging needs and opportunities
Facilitate working sessions with senior executives, including Sun Life’s Executive Team

People leadership and team development:

Manage a team of high-performing Directors & Senior Consultants
Mentor team members through apprenticeship and coaching
Foster a collaborative and learning-oriented team culture
Contribute to the development and success of the team and our practices

What do you need to succeed:

10+ years of relevant business experience, ideally within insurance or financial services
Strong understanding of at least one Sun Life business area (e.g. asset management, insurance, wealth management) and geographic markets (Canada, US, Asia)
Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills; able to effectively collaborate with multiple stakeholders across multiple teams
Able to work independently on assignments with appropriate judgment
Ability to coach team members on projects, providing guidance on analysis and deliverables
Proven ability to lead and develop a small team of high-performing professionals, including guiding project execution, driving accountability, and conducting performance and career development conversations

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
